Six math clues · answer key

A zipper clicks together.

Grade 2 math. Compare tens before ones. For rounding, 0–4 rounds down and 5–9 rounds up.

Math 1 · 46
38 < 46. 4 tens are more than 3 tens, so the greater count is 46.
Math 2 · 72
72 > 27. 7 tens are more than 2 tens, so the greater count is 72.
Math 3 · 54
54 = 54. Both rows have the shared count 54.
Math 4 · 40
43 has 3 ones, so it rounds down to 40.
Math 5 · 70
67 has 7 ones, so it rounds up to 70.
Math 6 · 100
95 has 5 ones, so it rounds up to 100.
Grade 2 math. The six tasks include comparison with <, >, and = plus nearest-ten rounding, including the 5-rounds-up rule. All counts are invented for the math story.
Grown-ups only · Welcome words, drawings, and second looks.
WONDER DAILY AGE 8 · GRADE 3 · ANSWERS · 2 / 2

Reading & writing · answer key

A zipper clicks together.

Reading · 1
Below the slider the rows are separate; above it they are joined. The boundary moves with the slider, showing that it guides the change.
Reading · 2
Closing sends separate rows through two channels toward one exit. Opening sends one joined row toward the center wedge and out through two channels.
Reading · 3
Each element locks with its neighbors at the center, but the many small connections and fabric tapes can still bend as a chain.
Writing
A spoken, dictated, drawn, or written explanation counts. Example: “The Y-shaped channel guides two tooth rows into one interlocked row.”
Use a clean, intact zipper on a pouch or jacket. Move it slowly while keeping fingers, hair, and loose fabric away from the slider. Do not take a slider apart or handle broken metal teeth. Zipper types differ: this pack shows an enlarged, simplified molded-tooth zipper. The teeth are more precisely called elements. A slider has internal guide channels and a central post or wedge; moving one way brings the rows into interlocking engagement, while moving the other way separates them. Stops keep the slider from leaving the chain. Some sliders also have a small locking part, but that extra mechanism is outside this lesson.

About 15 min. Accept invented spelling, speech, dictation, or a labeled drawing. One clear cause-and-effect idea is enough.
